questions.prompt: What is the role of the 'abstraction layer' in the core banking modernization journey?

options.text: It decouples the legacy system from the applications and ensures business continuity during coexistence
It replaces all microservices with a monolith

questions.explanation: The abstraction layer decouples the legacy mainframe from applications and ensures functional synchronization and business continuity between mainframe and Vault.

questions.prompt: What is the main challenge addressed by the 'dual run' phase?

options.text: Ensuring consistency and synchronization between the legacy and new cloud systems

questions.explanation: Dual run ensures the legacy mainframe and the new Vault system produce identical results for all operations, addressed via a passive pipeline, automated comparison, monitoring and stress testing.

questions.prompt: Which technologies underpin the new digital bank's transaction processing solution?
questions.explanation: The solution leverages a microservices architecture with Apache Flink and Apache Kafka for transaction processing, data validation, and legacy interfacing.

questions.prompt: The evolution roadmap is structured into three macro steps: abstraction layer, dual run, and customer migration.
questions.explanation: The three macro steps are: creating the abstraction layer (decoupling), the dual-run layer (coexistence), and migration of customers (definitive transition).

questions.prompt: In the Vault-based platform, what is the basic unit used to handle a product's business logic?
questions.explanation: Smart contracts are the basic unit of the Vault platform used to handle product business logic.

questions.prompt: Why are integration microservices placed as a facade in front of Vault?

options.text: Data transformation between Vault and other components
Extended functionality not present in Vault
To remove the need for any APIs

questions.explanation: The microservices facade enables data transformation, extended functionality, and performance optimization (local caching to reduce direct Vault requests).

questions.prompt: In the reverse-engineering analysis, what does 'dependency mapping' involve?

options.text: Analyzing interactions among front-end, back-end, database, and third-party systems

questions.explanation: Dependency mapping analyzes interactions among FE, BE, database, and third-party systems and creates a detailed map of integrations highlighting critical points.

questions.prompt: A dual-run architecture lets the old system keep operating alongside the new system to allow gradual migration and testing.
questions.explanation: The dual-run architecture keeps the old system running alongside the new one, enabling gradual migration and process testing before full transition.

questions.prompt: What does the 'Copy Banking' component do in the abstraction layer?

options.text: Subscribes to the results topics and replicates core entities into an external database

questions.explanation: Copy Banking subscribes to results topics and replicates core entities in an external DB, eliminating direct API calls, enabling custom indexes, and allowing per-channel entity shaping.

questions.prompt: In the update flow, how do microservices interact with the core through Kafka?

options.text: They publish requests to specific Kafka topics; the core processes them and publishes responses to a dedicated results topic each channel subscribes to
They call the mainframe directly via SOAP only
They write directly into the mainframe database
They poll a shared file system

questions.explanation: Microservices publish requests to Kafka topics; the core processes them and publishes responses to a dedicated results topic that the calling channel subscribes to.

questions.prompt: Which priorities are highlighted in the project's conclusions?

options.text: Optimization of the service (reducing MIPS consumption and costs)
Cutting-edge tech with AI embedded across SDLC phases

questions.explanation: The conclusions point to optimizing the service (lower MIPS/cost), cutting-edge tech (AI across the SDLC), and expanding high-interest functionalities.

questions.prompt: The group-wide core banking modernization involved 40+ Reply resources and migrating over 100 existing products from the legacy system to Vault.
questions.explanation: The modernization project involved 40+ Reply resources, a bank with 14M+ customers and 3k+ branches, and migration of over 100 products to Vault.

questions.prompt: During the analysis phase, what is the goal of 'code decomposition'?

options.text: Break the system into modules/components to identify key logic and critical issues
Delete the legacy source code immediately

questions.explanation: Code decomposition breaks the system into modules/components to identify key logic, assess complexity, analyze functional flows, and highlight reusable or obsolete functionality.

questions.prompt: Which GenAI-based accelerator is cited for daily developer support, from feature implementation to code testing?
questions.explanation: GitHub Copilot is cited as a potential GenAI accelerator for daily developer support, from feature implementation through code testing.

questions.prompt: What kind of group is Reply, as described in the deck?

options.text: A group (founded 1996) specialized in Consulting, System Integration, and Digital Services

questions.explanation: Reply, founded in 1996, is a group specialized in Consulting, System Integration, and Digital Services, with a focus on designing and implementing innovative solutions.

questions.prompt: Which phases make up the AI-enhanced end-to-end delivery approach?
questions.explanation: The delivery approach runs Analysis → Test Case Definition → Development → Certification → Release and Monitoring, under overall project governance, with GenAI accelerators.

questions.prompt: Which are key pillars of the dual-run solution?

options.text: A passive pipeline that duplicates accounts, balances, and transactions with no external impact
A recording pipeline duplicating transactions from the abstraction layer
A dedicated reconciliation tool comparing production and passive pipeline outputs

questions.explanation: Dual-run pillars: a passive (no-impact) pipeline, a recording pipeline duplicating abstraction-layer transactions, and a reconciliation tool comparing production vs passive outputs.

questions.prompt: What is the first step of the migration workflow (CWE)?

options.text: Mainframe extract — extracting balances, accounting entries with future dates, and availability blocks
Rollout of all accounts at once

questions.explanation: The migration begins with a mainframe extract (balances, future-dated accounting entries, availability blocks), followed by transcoding, load into core, bucket unloads, and reconciliation.

questions.prompt: Which figures describe the new digital bank at the time of the deck?

options.text: More than 500k customers, ~30k accounts opened per month, over 400k daily transactions

questions.explanation: The new digital bank had 500k+ customers, ~30k accounts opened per month, and over 400k daily transactions (the 14M-customer figure refers to the later group-wide modernization).
